faq.ue.title: UE Computer Engineering Program
faq.admissions.title: Admissions & Careers
faq.q1: What is the difference between Computer Engineering and Computer Science?
faq.a1: Computer Engineering integrates electrical engineering and computer science, focusing on the hardware-software interface. Computer Science focuses primarily on software, algorithms, and theoretical computing.
faq.a2: No. Computer Engineering covers both hardware and software. While you study digital logic, computer architecture, and electronics, you also learn firmware development, device drivers, real-time operating systems, and hardware-software co-design.
faq.q3: Do Computer Engineering students learn programming?
faq.a3: Yes. Programming is fundamental to Computer Engineering. You will learn C, C++, and Assembly for low-level and embedded programming, as well as Python, Java, or other languages for higher-level applications and tools.
faq.q4: What programming languages are commonly used?
faq.a4: Commonly used languages: C/C++ for embedded systems, firmware, real-time systems; Python for scripting, data analysis, ML/AI, testing; Verilog/VHDL for digital logic design, FPGA development; Assembly for microcontroller programming, optimization; Java/JavaScript for applications, web interfaces for embedded systems; MATLAB for signal processing, control systems.
faq.q5: What are the program educational objectives of UE BSCpE?
faq.a5: The UE BSCpE program aims to produce graduates who are: (1) professionally competent and globally competitive; (2) equipped with technical competencies to contribute to the country's social and economic progress; (3) lifelong learners imbued with UE core values of Excellence, Integrity, Professionalism, Teamwork, Commitment, Transparency, Accountability, and Social Responsibility.
faq.q6: What is the accreditation status of the program?
faq.a6: The UE Caloocan BSCpE program is PAASCU Level III Re-Accredited. The UE Manila BSCpE program holds PACUCOA Level II Candidate Status.
faq.q7: What is the focus of the UE CpE curriculum?
faq.a7: The UE CpE curriculum focuses on embedded systems — devices that use microprocessors or microcontrollers for specific purposes. The program balances engineering science and design, with hands-on projects starting from freshman year.
faq.a8: UE CpE application domains include: Multimedia, Aerospace & Avionics, Automotive, Consumer Electronics, Medical Sciences, Internet, Entertainment, Game System Hardware, Electronic Toys, Virtual Reality Hardware, Human Interface Devices, and Military.
faq.q9: What careers can CpE graduates pursue?
faq.a9: UE lists these career paths: Project Engineer/Manager, Network System Administrator/Manager, Data Communications Engineer, Systems Engineer/Developer/Manager, Systems Analyst/Designer, Technical Support Engineer/Manager, Test Engineer, Technopreneur, Software Engineer, Educator and Researcher. Additional industry roles include Embedded Systems Engineer, IoT Engineer, Hardware Engineer, Cybersecurity Engineer, AI/ML Engineer, Cloud Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Robotics Engineer, and R&D Engineer.
faq.q10: What skills should incoming CpE students develop?
faq.a10: Strong foundation in mathematics (calculus, discrete math, linear algebra); Physics fundamentals (electricity, magnetism, mechanics); Basic programming experience (any language); Logical thinking and problem-solving skills; Interest in how hardware and software interact; Willingness to learn circuit analysis and digital logic.
faq.q11: What is the licensure examination for Computer Engineers?
faq.a11: In the Philippines, Computer Engineering graduates take the Computer Engineering Licensure Examination administered by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC). UE Manila reported a first-timers passing rate of 93.33% in the 2025 Electrical Engineers Licensure Exam (which includes CpE).

whatIs.hwsw.integration.title: Where They Meet: Hardware-Software Integration
whatIs.hwsw.integration.desc: The defining skill of a Computer Engineer is co-design — making hardware and software decisions together to optimize for performance, power, cost, and reliability. This systems-level thinking is what distinguishes Computer Engineering from its parent disciplines.
whatIs.fields.intro: Computer Engineering spans multiple interconnected fields. Students typically build depth in one or more of these areas through electives, projects, and research.
whatIs.fields.item1.topics: Key topics: Microcontrollers, RTOS, C/C++, bare-metal programming
whatIs.fields.item1.apps: Applications: Automotive ECUs, medical devices, IoT sensors, industrial controllers
whatIs.fields.item2.topics: Key topics: ISA design, pipelining, cache hierarchy, parallel processing
whatIs.fields.item2.apps: Applications: CPU/GPU design, high-performance computing, accelerator chips
whatIs.fields.item3.topics: Key topics: Verilog/VHDL, FPGA, ASIC flow, timing analysis
whatIs.fields.item3.apps: Applications: Custom SoCs, AI accelerators, memory controllers, I/O interfaces
whatIs.fields.item4.topics: Key topics: TCP/IP, routing, switching, network security, QoS
whatIs.fields.item4.apps: Applications: Data centers, 5G/6G, IoT connectivity, SDN/NFV
whatIs.fields.item5.topics: Key topics: DSP algorithms, filters, transforms, real-time processing
whatIs.fields.item5.apps: Applications: Wireless comms, audio/video codecs, radar/sonar, biomedical imaging
whatIs.fields.item6.topics: Key topics: Control theory, sensor fusion, ROS, real-time control loops
whatIs.fields.item6.apps: Applications: Industrial robots, autonomous vehicles, drones, surgical robots
whatIs.do.intro: Computer Engineers work across the full lifecycle of computing systems. Their work typically spans these core activities:
whatIs.do.note: Note: The specific mix of activities varies by role. An embedded engineer might spend 80% of their time on firmware development, while a hardware engineer focuses on circuit design and verification. Computer Engineering's breadth allows graduates to specialize based on interest.
whatIs.vsCS.title: Computer Engineering vs. Computer Science
whatIs.vsCS.intro: Both disciplines work with computing, but they differ in focus and scope:
whatIs.vsCS.row1.cpe: Hardware–software interface; systems that integrate both
whatIs.vsCS.row2.cpe: Deep: circuits, architecture, digital logic, VLSI
whatIs.vsCS.row3.cs: Broad: applications, systems, web, AI/ML, theory
whatIs.vsCS.row5.cpe: Chips, boards, embedded devices, real-time systems
whatIs.vsCS.conclusion: In practice, the fields overlap significantly. Many Computer Engineers write substantial software, and many Computer Scientists work with hardware. Choose Computer Engineering if you want to understand and design the complete computing system — from the physics of transistors to the software that runs on them.
